title: Hosted Inference v3: Streaming, Batch Fusion, and Fidelity Telemetry — Release Notes
author: Marisol Vega
body:
Summary
-------
Hosted Inference v3 (HIF-v3) is a major platform release focused on three customer-facing improvements: stable streaming semantics across modes, Batch Fusion (an adaptive microbatching optimization), and per-request fidelity telemetry for production quality signals. This release targets hosted API customers and is the foundation for Dedicated/Private parity in Q1 2029.

Highlights
----------
- Stable streaming API with exactly-once token ordering guarantees for streamed fragments and improved backpressure handling.
- Batch Fusion: runtime-level microbatcher that merges low-latency single-shot requests into short-lived fused batches to improve GPU utilization without increasing tail latency for latency-sensitive routes.
- Fidelity Telemetry: per-request quality metadata (model_variant, quantization_profile, prompt_hash, eval_flag) surfaced through console and streaming headers for downstream quality monitoring and automated rollback triggers.
- Backwards-compatible client surface: existing REST and SDK calls continue to work; new optional flags enable v3 behaviors.
- Operational improvements: new dashboards (hosted.hif.v3.*) and alerting templates for fidelity regressions.

Compatibility and API diff
------------------------
- Existing endpoints remain available. Two optional query parameters and one response header are added: 
  - request_param: streaming_mode=v3 (string; optional) — toggles new streaming engine.
  - request_param: batch_fusion=auto|on|off (string; default=auto) — controls Batch Fusion heuristic.
  - response_header: X-Redwood-Fidelity-Telemetry (JSON blob) — present when fidelity telemetry is enabled for the tenant.

Example request (curl):

curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate?streaming_mode=v3 \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY' \n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n  -d '{"model":"rw-v3-1b","input":"Summarize the following...","batch_fusion":"auto"}'

Example response header (abbreviated):
X-Redwood-Fidelity-Telemetry: {"model_variant":"rw-v3-1b.q4_0","quant_profile":"econ-1","prompt_hash":"a3f2...","eval_flag":"baseline:2028-10-12"}

Behavioral changes and guarantees
--------------------------------
1. Streaming ordering: HIF-v3 guarantees that tokens emitted by the server for a single request maintain strict ordering and are idempotent across reconnects. If a client reconnects mid-stream using the resume_token returned in the initial stream preamble, the runtime will re-stream only the missing suffix.
2. Backpressure: the client SDKs expose a small-buffer consumer that avoids head-of-line blocking for long-running streams. Node/Python SDKs updated in SDK 4.x.
3. Batch Fusion heuristics: default 'auto' mode fuses compatible small requests within a 4–12 ms window depending on workload. Auto-mode aims to improve tokens/s on V100/A100-class instances by ~18–40% on conversational workloads while preserving 99th percentile latency targets for routes configured with latency_slo < 200ms.

SLOs and Performance (hosted tier guidance)
-------------------------------------------
- Median token latency: unchanged; measured per-customer baseline.
- 95th percentile latency impact (expected): +0–15ms for batch-fusion benefitting routes; customers with strict 95th latency SLOs should set batch_fusion=off on those routes.
- Throughput gain: 18–40% tokens/sec for small-request conversational mixes (see performance appendix).
- Fidelity telemetry delivery SLA: metadata header included for >99.9% of streaming/generate responses in hosted control planes.

Upgrade and migration notes
--------------------------
- No forced client upgrade: default server behavior remains legacy-compatible. Tenants should opt-in to streaming_mode=v3 to enable new behavior.
- Recommended steps for production rollout: 
  1. Opt-in a single low-traffic route (canary) with streaming_mode=v3 and batch_fusion=auto. Monitor latency and fidelity dashboards for 48–72h.
  2. If 95th latency increases beyond acceptable thresholds, switch batch_fusion=off for that route and open a support ticket.
  3. Enable fidelity telemetry to capture prompt_hash and quant_profile across a representative prompt set. Tie telemetry to existing quality monitors (Eval Runner / QA webhooks).
  4. Gradually expand to more routes and/or set batch_fusion=on where throughput matters more than tail latency (e.g., offline batch generation).

Configuration matrix (recommended defaults)
-----------------------------------------
| Route type | streaming_mode | batch_fusion | recommended | notes |
|------------|----------------|--------------|-------------|-------|
| Low-latency interactive | v3 | off | keep tail latency | Avoid fusion for sub-100ms 95th SLOs |
| Conversational chat | v3 | auto | default | Auto fusion improves throughput while preserving latency for most workloads |
| Bulk generation | legacy | on | maximize throughput | Use batch_fusion=on with larger window for bulk jobs |

Note: the table above is provided as ASCII for Confluence rendering; console shows same options in per-route settings UI.

Observability and telemetry
--------------------------
- New metrics emitted (prefix hosted.hif.v3):
  - hosted.hif.v3.batch_fusion.mean_batch_size
  - hosted.hif.v3.batch_fusion.window_ms
  - hosted.hif.v3.streaming.resume_rate
  - hosted.hif.v3.fidelity.mismatches (counts of eval regression flags)
- Console: per-route Fidelity Panel shows prompt_hash heatmaps, quality regression alerts, and drift timelines.
- Alerting templates: fidelity-regression-high (threshold: fidelity.mismatches > 0.5% over 24h) and batch-fusion-latency-regression (95th latency increase > 20% vs baseline).

Rollout plan and risk mitigation
--------------------------------
- Phased rollout over 6 weeks: 
  - Week 0: internal dogfood and integration tests with SDK teams.
  - Weeks 1–2: opt-in canary tenants (low traffic).
  - Weeks 3–4: broaden to self-serve tenants with console toggle.
  - Weeks 5–6: auto-promote to default for conversational routes (metrics permitting).
- Rollback strategy: server-side toggle for streaming_mode and batch_fusion per-tenant and per-route. Escape hatch: global disable for HIF-v3 if systemic issue detected.

Known issues and workarounds
---------------------------
- Intermittent duplicate stream fragments during early canary when network jitter + resume_token mismatch occur. Workaround: client should dedupe by sequence number (SDKs handle this automatically in 4.2.1+).
- Some older SDK versions do not surface the X-Redwood-Fidelity-Telemetry header. Action: upgrade to SDK 4.2.1 or parse telemetry from the console API.

Developer and partner notes
---------------------------
- SDK changes: Node and Python SDKs include a new StreamClient.resume(stream_id, resume_token) helper and a Telemetry.parseHeader(header_str) utility. See SDK changelog for usage examples.
- Partner integrations: marketplace partners who rely on token-level metering should verify billing hooks when fidelity headers are enabled. Contact partner-ops@redwood.ai for an integration checklist.

Appendix A — Performance summary (selected benchmarks)
-----------------------------------------------------
- Conversational mix (50–100 token responses, median request size 32 tokens): A100-hosted pool saw +28% tokens/sec with batch_fusion=auto; 95th latency delta +9ms.
- Single-shot summarization (median 512 tokens): negligible fusion benefit; prefer legacy path.

Appendix B — API examples and JSON schemas
------------------------------------------
Request body example:
{
  "model":"rw-v3-1b",
  "input":"Write a short onboarding checklist for a new engineer.",
  "streaming_mode":"v3",
  "batch_fusion":"auto",
  "meta": {"route_id":"team-chat-1"}
}

Response header example (HTTP):
X-Redwood-Fidelity-Telemetry: {"model_variant":"rw-v3-1b.q4_0","quant_profile":"econ-1","prompt_hash":"a3f2...","eval_flag":"baseline:2028-10-12"}

FAQ
---
Q: Will enabling fidelity telemetry increase request cost?
A: No. Fidelity metadata is a lightweight header and is free at the control-plane level. Some customers may choose to store telemetry in long-term logs (costs depend on retention).

Q: Does Batch Fusion change model outputs?
A: No, Batch Fusion is a scheduling optimization and preserves per-request KV cache isolation and decoding determinism. We include reproducibility checks in the rollout.
